description:
Piracy Reworked

v0.1.0 - the underworld runs on your money - for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

In vanilla, trading with the transponder off has literally zero consequences - and the moment you stop needing the black market, pirates stop mattering. This mod does neither of those things. It doesn't punish you for smuggling; it makes the pirates

spend your money

. And it gives a rich late-game captain reasons to keep dealing with the underworld long after the black market's prices stop being interesting.

Piracy Reworked

is standalone and vanilla-only: a closed-loop pirate war economy you can bankroll, contain, or burn to the ground.

Download

PiracyReworked-0.1.0.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher. Safe to add to an existing save.

The war chest

Every black market transaction - buys and sells, transponder on or off (the authorities may not see you, but the pirates are the counterparty) - feeds a sector-wide pirate war chest. Sales are valued at actual demand-adjusted credits and weighted by usefulness to a war effort: weapons x3, ships x2, commodities x1, ore x0.5, and a flat bonus for blueprints on top of the vanilla behavior. Wash-trading nets to zero.

The chest is a real economy, not a difficulty slider:

Operating bases earn passive income - tuned to sustain their vanilla raid cadence, no more.Launching a raid costs the chest credits per fleet point. A broke underworld doesn't sail.A successful raid pays spoils back with interest; a repelled raid is a pure loss.When the chest covers the next base's cost, the pirates expand - bases are priced by tier (~94k to ~614k), and a flush underworld builds strongholds while a poor one rebuilds with wrecks.

The strategic grammar:

smuggle

and the underworld snowballs.

Repel raids

and it stagnates at break-even.

Hunt bases

and it shrinks - each kill destroys the pirates' investment and their income.

The underworld tithe

The underworld also collects a monthly cut of the

sector's

illegal trade - the same commodity flows vanilla routes as smuggling fleets, counted at both ends of every run. Income that scales with the size of the economy instead of your personal habits, so pirates stay financed late game even if you never fence another crate.

Your colonies are clients whether you like it or not: a big colony's drug and organ demand is met by smuggling into it, and your markets' share of the tithe gets its own intel line. Free ports - anyone's, yours included - fence at a multiplier. Free Port finally has an underworld price tag.

Wipe out every base and only a trickle flows. Eradication buys years of quiet - but piracy follows interstellar civilization, and the trickle eventually re-founds a base.

The broker

Underworld-tagged

contacts

offer, alongside their regular job list, to have things

sourced

:

Industrial equipment - real theft. The menu lists colony items actually installed at NPC colonies, each entry naming its source. The price carries a danger premium scaled to the source's real defenses, and a source the network's best base can't crack shows greyed out - feed the war chest and the menu opens up. On success the item is removed from the victim colony's industry. Theft, not manufacture.Blueprints. A small rotating monthly menu of rare blueprints liberated from faction archives - and of course the pirates keep a copy for themselves.

Full deposit up front, straight into the war chest - and it counts as your personal patronage in full. Fulfillment is a

real raid

by an operating pirate base, resolved by the actual raid sim against the target's actual defenses. Repelled raid: half back. No bases at all? The broker still deals - your deposit is quite literally financing the reconstruction that will fulfill it.

Access works the way vanilla contacts work: the option appears at Favorable rep, and the network's reach scales with the contact's importance - the crown jewels need a well-placed contact. Money spent on vanilla underworld contact jobs (custom production markups, hand-me-down freighters) feeds the chest the same way.

Fading wariness

Piracy Respite - vanilla's permanent reward for beating the pirate crisis - says pirates are

wary

of attacking you. Wariness fades when the war chest overflows with your own money: past the thresholds (500k lifetime / 25% share by default), chest-funded bases resume preying on your colonies - the vanilla pirate activity condition, never raids. Your share dilutes as the underworld earns its own money, so laying off eventually restores the respite - and hunting pirates offsets your ledger directly.

A price on your head

Factions whose markets you smuggle through post

personal

bounties - no faction rep consequences, nothing can be proven well enough for open hostilities. Accrual is gated on the market's vanilla smuggling suspicion: transponder-off trading generates none; brazen trading gets you posted. Commissioning a raid through the broker adds a cut of the deposit to the victim's ledger - a raid is loud.

The ledgers are per faction - you buy your way off each list separately, at a premium - but the hunters are freelancers who collect from every poster at once, and everything on their side works off the

combined

price:

The pool activates once it clears the floor and funds hunters worth taking on your current fleet. A formidable fleet deters hunters - but the deterrence is uncapped in reverse, and a big enough price always finds takers.While too small to draw hunters, every ledger festers at a higher rate. Ignoring a small price on your head only lets it ripen.A throwaway decoy fleet freezes the bounty instead - the contract is your fleet destroyed, and nobody burns a hunt on a worthless prize.Hunter fleets scale with the pool, up to several hunting concurrently - and destroying one raises every poster's bounty. No rep impact either way.

And the rest

Tier 3+ bases field extra medium/heavy patrols, bigger fleets, and a tier-scaled garrison - a tier 5 base is a fortress, not a bare station.The "Pirate War Chest" intel screen is a full balance sheet: chest, income streams, operating bases, savings toward the next base, the recent ledger - and exactly how much of the pirate war economy you bankrolled.Machine factions (the Remnants and their like) are outside the underworld economy: no tithe, no commission raids against them, no bounties from them.Kept vanilla: per-base raid strength and cadence, tier progression, station restoration, the post-kill respawn freeze, the first-year grace period.

Configuration

Everything above is tunable. With

LunaLib

enabled (optional) you get a live in-game settings menu - rates, thresholds, weights, caps, all of it. Without LunaLib the mod reads the same values from data/config/settings.json and runs fine standalone.

Requirements & compatibility

Starsector 0.98a-RC8LunaLib - optional, for the in-game config menuVanilla-only - no other hard dependenciesSafe to add to an existing save: existing raiding bases are adopted as-isColony-crisis bases, Hostile Activity, Kanta's Protection and Piracy Respite are untouchedOverrides the cpc/hmdf rows of person_missions.csv with subclasses (behavior unchanged) - flag if another mod edits those

Changelog

v0.1.0

Initial release.

Recommended mod collection for ultimate late game experience

Standalone, vanilla-only, safe to add mid-save — designed to stack.

Threat Incursion (v0.2.0) — the swarm colonizes the sector and raids the core worlds. Disrupt their supplies chains and steal their fabrication cores.
Commerce Wars (v0.2.0) — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.
Piracy Reworked (v0.1.0) — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.
Remnant Retribution (v0.3.1) — a late-game colony crisis: prosper too hard and the Remnant come to collect.
Useful Planetary Shield (v0.1.2) — planetary shields finally do something: they absorb orbital bombardment.

Disclaimer: This post and these mods were written using Claude's Fable AI model. Design and testing by pogoman.

Piracy Reworked
v0.1.0 - the underworld runs on your money - for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

In vanilla, trading with the transponder off has literally zero consequences - and the moment you stop needing the black market, pirates stop mattering. This mod does neither of those things. It doesn't punish you for smuggling; it makes the pirates spend your money. And it gives a rich late-game captain reasons to keep dealing with the underworld long after the black market's prices stop being interesting.

Piracy Reworked is standalone and vanilla-only: a closed-loop pirate war economy you can bankroll, contain, or burn to the ground.


Download

PiracyReworked-0.1.0.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher. Safe to add to an existing save.


The war chest

Every black market transaction - buys and sells, transponder on or off (the authorities may not see you, but the pirates are the counterparty) - feeds a sector-wide pirate war chest. Sales are valued at actual demand-adjusted credits and weighted by usefulness to a war effort: weapons x3, ships x2, commodities x1, ore x0.5, and a flat bonus for blueprints on top of the vanilla behavior. Wash-trading nets to zero.
The chest is a real economy, not a difficulty slider:
  • Operating bases earn passive income - tuned to sustain their vanilla raid cadence, no more.
  • Launching a raid costs the chest credits per fleet point. A broke underworld doesn't sail.
  • A successful raid pays spoils back with interest; a repelled raid is a pure loss.
  • When the chest covers the next base's cost, the pirates expand - bases are priced by tier (~94k to ~614k), and a flush underworld builds strongholds while a poor one rebuilds with wrecks.

The strategic grammar: smuggle and the underworld snowballs. Repel raids and it stagnates at break-even. Hunt bases and it shrinks - each kill destroys the pirates' investment and their income.


The underworld tithe

The underworld also collects a monthly cut of the sector's illegal trade - the same commodity flows vanilla routes as smuggling fleets, counted at both ends of every run. Income that scales with the size of the economy instead of your personal habits, so pirates stay financed late game even if you never fence another crate.

Your colonies are clients whether you like it or not: a big colony's drug and organ demand is met by smuggling into it, and your markets' share of the tithe gets its own intel line. Free ports - anyone's, yours included - fence at a multiplier. Free Port finally has an underworld price tag.

Wipe out every base and only a trickle flows. Eradication buys years of quiet - but piracy follows interstellar civilization, and the trickle eventually re-founds a base.


The broker

Underworld-tagged contacts offer, alongside their regular job list, to have things sourced:

  • Industrial equipment - real theft. The menu lists colony items actually installed at NPC colonies, each entry naming its source. The price carries a danger premium scaled to the source's real defenses, and a source the network's best base can't crack shows greyed out - feed the war chest and the menu opens up. On success the item is removed from the victim colony's industry. Theft, not manufacture.
  • Blueprints. A small rotating monthly menu of rare blueprints liberated from faction archives - and of course the pirates keep a copy for themselves.

Full deposit up front, straight into the war chest - and it counts as your personal patronage in full. Fulfillment is a real raid by an operating pirate base, resolved by the actual raid sim against the target's actual defenses. Repelled raid: half back. No bases at all? The broker still deals - your deposit is quite literally financing the reconstruction that will fulfill it.

Access works the way vanilla contacts work: the option appears at Favorable rep, and the network's reach scales with the contact's importance - the crown jewels need a well-placed contact. Money spent on vanilla underworld contact jobs (custom production markups, hand-me-down freighters) feeds the chest the same way.


Fading wariness

Piracy Respite - vanilla's permanent reward for beating the pirate crisis - says pirates are wary of attacking you. Wariness fades when the war chest overflows with your own money: past the thresholds (500k lifetime / 25% share by default), chest-funded bases resume preying on your colonies - the vanilla pirate activity condition, never raids. Your share dilutes as the underworld earns its own money, so laying off eventually restores the respite - and hunting pirates offsets your ledger directly.


A price on your head

Factions whose markets you smuggle through post personal bounties - no faction rep consequences, nothing can be proven well enough for open hostilities. Accrual is gated on the market's vanilla smuggling suspicion: transponder-off trading generates none; brazen trading gets you posted. Commissioning a raid through the broker adds a cut of the deposit to the victim's ledger - a raid is loud.

The ledgers are per faction - you buy your way off each list separately, at a premium - but the hunters are freelancers who collect from every poster at once, and everything on their side works off the combined price:

  • The pool activates once it clears the floor and funds hunters worth taking on your current fleet. A formidable fleet deters hunters - but the deterrence is uncapped in reverse, and a big enough price always finds takers.
  • While too small to draw hunters, every ledger festers at a higher rate. Ignoring a small price on your head only lets it ripen.
  • A throwaway decoy fleet freezes the bounty instead - the contract is your fleet destroyed, and nobody burns a hunt on a worthless prize.
  • Hunter fleets scale with the pool, up to several hunting concurrently - and destroying one raises every poster's bounty. No rep impact either way.


And the rest

  • Tier 3+ bases field extra medium/heavy patrols, bigger fleets, and a tier-scaled garrison - a tier 5 base is a fortress, not a bare station.
  • The "Pirate War Chest" intel screen is a full balance sheet: chest, income streams, operating bases, savings toward the next base, the recent ledger - and exactly how much of the pirate war economy you bankrolled.
  • Machine factions (the Remnants and their like) are outside the underworld economy: no tithe, no commission raids against them, no bounties from them.
  • Kept vanilla: per-base raid strength and cadence, tier progression, station restoration, the post-kill respawn freeze, the first-year grace period.


Configuration

Everything above is tunable. With LunaLib enabled (optional) you get a live in-game settings menu - rates, thresholds, weights, caps, all of it. Without LunaLib the mod reads the same values from data/config/settings.json and runs fine standalone.


Requirements & compatibility

  • Starsector 0.98a-RC8
  • LunaLib - optional, for the in-game config menu
  • Vanilla-only - no other hard dependencies
  • Safe to add to an existing save: existing raiding bases are adopted as-is
  • Colony-crisis bases, Hostile Activity, Kanta's Protection and Piracy Respite are untouched
  • Overrides the cpc/hmdf rows of person_missions.csv with subclasses (behavior unchanged) - flag if another mod edits those

  • Threat Incursion (v0.2.0) — the swarm colonizes the sector and raids the core worlds. Disrupt their supplies chains and steal their fabrication cores.
  • Commerce Wars (v0.2.0) — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.
  • Piracy Reworked (v0.1.0) — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.
  • Remnant Retribution (v0.3.1) — a late-game colony crisis: prosper too hard and the Remnant come to collect.
  • Useful Planetary Shield (v0.1.2) — planetary shields finally do something: they absorb orbital bombardment.
